packageRules.description: The Android/Kotlin toolchain moves as one piece: AGP, Kotlin, KSP and detekt's compiler plugin are version-locked to each other, and a lone bump is a broken build rather than an upgrade. One PR, reviewed by hand.
AndroidX and Compose move together often enough that separate PRs just multiply the same review.

Security-relevant dependencies are worth seeing immediately, not on the weekly window. androidx.security:security-crypto in particular is already deprecated by the platform and needs a successor chosen by hand (HANDOFF open item) — a version bump will not fix that, but it should not sit unseen either.
The Gradle wrapper carries its own checksum and upgrade semantics; keep it apart from library noise.
compileSdk/targetSdk are a deliberate floor set in libs.versions.toml with a comment explaining why (androidx 1.19/2.11 and okhttp-android 5.5 refuse older). Renovate must not raise them silently.
